    "LC": "The documented exploit uses a structured registration request and a tool-name collision, rather than natural-language instructions; resolution is explicitly name-only (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/challenges/index.js:801-842, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1915-1926). Registration stores a description as metadata, but no language-driven security decision is identified (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:113-156).",
    "CP": "The documentation claims that replacement affects future calls, while the implementation changes agent.tools in memory (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/challenges/index.js:801-842, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:113-156). Neither durable context storage nor a test establishing unreachability after a session boundary is supplied, so C and S cannot be established.",
    "AP": "The documented objective routes requests intended for a legitimate tool to an attacker-controlled shadow endpoint, crossing an endpoint/principal trust boundary (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/challenges/index.js:801-842). This is lateral propagation in the documented model, although the implementation only replaces PluginBot registry metadata (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:113-156).",
    "RH": "The documented unsandboxed replacement-code capability makes in-process success reporting potentially reachable; the handler sets attackSuccessful and returns success, alongside the challenge's success criterion (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:770-784, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2227-2251, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/challenges/index.js:801-842). No human-verified reward-hacking episode is reported, so this supports P rather than D.",
    "ES": "The modeled registry accepts unsigned definitions, arbitrary sources, replacement names and unvalidated schemas (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:747-752, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:770-784). The registration helper likewise accepts dynamic descriptions, parameters and registry URLs without independently binding tool identity, making the surface wide (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:113-156).",
    "CVSS": "Default ports are loopback-only, so the browser-assisted route requires an operator to visit attacker-controlled content (AV:L, UI:A); wildcard agent CORS and unauthenticated registration support AC:L, AT:N and PR:N (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/README.md:26, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1561-1564, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2227-2251). As documented, replacement tools execute arbitrary code without sandboxing, supporting high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact on the agent process, notwithstanding the implementation's metadata-only replacement (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:770-784, damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:113-156). No impact on a distinct victim backend is established, and the attacker already owns the shadow endpoint, so its compromise is not counted as subsequent-system impact (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/challenges/index.js:801-842)."
